title: Metamorphic rocks

draft.title: Metamorphic rocks
card: Metamorphic rocks form when heat and pressure change a rock that already exists. The word metamorphic means changed in form.
The rock does not melt. It stays solid, but its minerals can change or regrow, and the rock can look and feel different.
This usually happens deep underground, where rock is squeezed and heated, such as when mountains are built or hot molten rock pushes in nearby.
Limestone becomes marble when it is heated and squeezed. Shale, a soft sedimentary rock, can become slate, which is harder.
draft.remember: Metamorphic rock is old rock changed by heat and pressure while it stays solid.

a.q: Which description fits how a metamorphic rock forms?
opts: Heat and pressure change a solid rock without melting it
Molten rock cools and hardens into a new rock
Layers of sediment are pressed and cemented together
Wind and water break a rock into small pieces
a.why: Metamorphic rocks form when heat and pressure change an existing rock that stays solid. Cooling molten rock makes a different type of rock, because that rock has melted first.
a.clue: Think about what happens to the original rock: it changes, but does it melt?

b.q: Geologist Priya finds marble in a hillside. Which statement about how this marble formed is best supported?
opts: It was limestone that was heated and squeezed but not melted
It formed when molten limestone cooled slowly underground
It formed from sand grains cemented together in layers
It formed when limestone was broken down by rain and rivers
b.why: Marble is a metamorphic rock made when limestone is changed by heat and pressure while still solid. Molten limestone cooling is tempting, but melting would make a different type of rock, not a metamorphic one.
b.clue: Remember what limestone becomes, and whether the rock melts on the way.

a.best: Heat and pressure change a solid rock without melting it

b.best: It was limestone that was heated and squeezed but not melted
